source_note: Compiled from official notices and mainstream reporting. Every card links to its original source.

items.title: New Zealand visa rules change for Indian travellers from 1 October 2026
items.summary: New Zealand is introducing changes to its visa rules for Indian travellers starting 1 October 2026. The update affects how Indians can apply for and obtain visas to visit New Zealand.

items.title: Australia student visa rejections surge, Indian applicants hit hard
items.summary: Student visa rejection rates in Australia have increased significantly, with Indian applicants particularly affected by the tougher approval standards. The surge represents a notable shift in Australia's student visa processing for Indian nationals.

items.title: Australia MATES Visa 2026: Eligibility, requirements, cost and how to apply
items.summary: Information is now available about Australia's MATES Visa programme for 2026, including who is eligible to apply, what requirements must be met, the costs involved, and the application process for this visa category.

items.title: Australia student visa refusal rate hits 10-year high for Indian applicants
items.summary: Australia's student visa refusal rate has reached its highest level in ten years, with applicants from India and Nepal facing particularly tough scrutiny during the assessment process. The increased rejection rate marks a significant tightening of student visa approvals.

items.title: EB-1 green card risk grows for Indians as visa numbers near annual limit
items.summary: Indian applicants for EB-1 green cards face growing uncertainty as the annual allocation of visa numbers approaches its limit. This development could affect processing timelines and availability for Indian nationals seeking permanent residency through this category.

items.title: Indians can visit UAE to seek jobs without local employer or sponsor
items.summary: Indians are now able to travel to the UAE to look for employment opportunities without requiring a local employer or sponsor in advance. This change makes it easier for Indian job seekers to explore work opportunities directly in the UAE.

items.title: New Zealand expands post-study work visa and launches 6-month graduate visa
items.summary: New Zealand is expanding eligibility for its Post-Study Work Visa and introducing a new six-month graduate work visa starting 16 November. The changes open up more work pathways for international graduates who have studied in New Zealand.

items.title: Trump moves to scrap H-1B visa 60-day grace period for Indian workers
items.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly moving to eliminate the 60-day grace period currently available to H-1B visa holders. This change would create new risks for Indian workers on H-1B visas who lose their jobs or need to transition between employers.

items.title: New Zealand ends paper visa applications for several categories from October
items.summary: New Zealand will discontinue paper-based visa applications for multiple visa categories starting in October. Applicants will need to use online application systems instead of submitting physical paperwork for these visa types.

items.title: Indians face growing US immigration hurdles under Trump administration
items.summary: Indian employees, students, dependants and visitors are reportedly encountering increased difficulties with US immigration processes under the Trump administration. The nature and extent of these hurdles affecting multiple visa categories is not specified in the report.

items.title: New Zealand to end paper visa applications for several categories in October
items.summary: From October, New Zealand will stop accepting paper applications for several visa categories, moving to digital-only processing. The change affects multiple visa types but specific categories are not listed in the report.

items.title: US suspends Cognizant's green card filings under PERM programme
items.summary: The United States has suspended Cognizant's ability to file green card applications through the PERM labour certification process. This development affects Indians working at Cognizant who are seeking permanent residency through employer sponsorship.

items.title: Canada allows foreign workers to take short courses without study permit
items.summary: Canada has eased study rules for foreign workers already in the country, permitting them to enrol in short courses without obtaining a separate study permit. This change simplifies access to training and education for temporary workers.

items.title: Indian students rethink the American dream amid visa uncertainty
items.summary: Indian students are reconsidering their plans to study in the United States due to growing uncertainty around visa policies. The changing immigration landscape is causing prospective students to evaluate their options more carefully before committing to American universities.

items.title: New Zealand visitor visa rules to change from October 2026
items.summary: New Zealand will introduce changes to visitor visa rules starting in October 2026. The specific nature of the rule changes has not been detailed in the report.

items.title: Cognizant suspends green card filings in US: Impact on workers
items.summary: Cognizant has suspended green card filings in the United States, which will affect workers employed by the company who were expecting employer-sponsored permanent residency applications. The suspension raises questions about the implications for current and prospective employees seeking long-term immigration status.

items.title: Trump's H-1B crackdown impacts Indian IT industry
items.summary: The H-1B visa crackdown under the Trump administration is affecting the Indian IT industry. While the measures are creating challenges for Indian technology workers and companies, the report suggests the industry had anticipated these restrictions and may have prepared accordingly.

items.title: US EB-1 green card category may become unavailable for Indians before September ends
items.summary: The EB-1 employment-based green card category for Indians is likely to become unavailable before September 30. This would affect Indian applicants seeking permanent residency through this priority category during the current fiscal year.

items.title: Canada announces student visa changes for 2026 affecting funds, PAL and co-op
items.summary: Canada has introduced changes to student visa rules for 2026 covering financial requirements, Provincial Attestation Letters and co-op programme regulations. The specific details of these changes are not outlined in the report.

items.title: Credit checks may impact US green card applicants and sponsors
items.summary: Credit checks could affect both green card applicants and their sponsors in the United States. The report suggests this financial scrutiny may add a new dimension to the permanent residency application process.

items.title: Canada study permit 2026: Higher funds, tighter scrutiny and new norms announced
items.summary: Canada has announced changes to study permit requirements for 2026, including increased financial proof requirements, stricter application scrutiny and new regulations for international students. The specific amounts and detailed norms are not provided.

items.title: Australian student visa refusals reach 10-year high
items.summary: Student visa refusals in Australia have hit their highest level in a decade, affecting applicants' educational plans. The report describes the situation as shattering dreams but does not specify refusal rates or reasons.

items.title: India introduces biometric kiosks to speed up immigration for e-Visa travellers
items.summary: India has deployed biometric kiosks at immigration checkpoints to accelerate processing for travellers arriving on e-Visas. The new system aims to reduce wait times and streamline entry procedures at Indian airports.

items.title: UK immigration rules changing from October: Five major updates
items.summary: The United Kingdom is implementing changes to its immigration rules starting in October. The report highlights five major updates that will affect visa applicants. Those planning to apply for UK visas should familiarize themselves with the new requirements taking effect next month.

items.title: US visa interviews available in 10 days for $750 fee
items.summary: A new US visa update allows applicants to schedule visa interviews within ten days by paying a fee of 750 dollars. This expedited service option may benefit those needing urgent appointments, though it comes at a significant additional cost beyond standard application fees.

items.title: US warns EB-1 green card category for Indians may run out before September 30
items.summary: The United States has issued an alert that the EB-1 green card category may be exhausted before the end of September. This affects Indian applicants seeking permanent residence through the employment-based first preference route, which typically serves priority workers.

items.title: US reportedly weighing H-1B changes including grace period and H-4 work authorization
items.summary: The United States is reportedly considering modifications to H-1B visa rules that could affect grace periods for job changes, fee structures and employment authorization for H-4 dependent visa holders. These potential changes would impact Indian workers and their families in America.

items.title: How Indians on US tourist visas can extend their stay using Form I-539
items.summary: Indians visiting the United States on tourist visas can apply to extend their stay using Form I-539. The process involves specific timing requirements and procedures for those wishing to remain longer than their initial authorized period.

items.title: Trump administration reportedly considering stricter H-1B and student visa rules
items.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly weighing tighter regulations for H-1B work visas, green cards, and student visas. These potential changes could significantly affect Indian applicants across multiple visa categories if implemented.

items.title: New Zealand student visa processing times for 2027 intake
items.summary: Information about student visa processing times for New Zealand has been released for students planning to begin studies in 2027. The update provides guidance for Indian students preparing applications for New Zealand educational institutions.

items.title: Can Indians work in Canada on a visitor visa? Rules on jobs and penalties explained
items.summary: The article clarifies Canadian regulations regarding employment on visitor visas. It explains what work is permitted, when separate work permits are required, and the penalties Indians may face for working illegally while in Canada on visitor status without proper authorization.

items.title: UK student visa fees increasing from November 2026 for Indian applicants
items.summary: The cost of obtaining a UK student visa will rise starting November 2026. Indian students planning to study in the United Kingdom need to factor in these higher fees when budgeting for their education abroad and preparing their visa applications.

items.title: UAE Golden Visa eligibility: What Indians need to know about the ₹5 crore threshold
items.summary: The article examines whether an investment of five crore rupees qualifies Indians for the UAE Golden Visa programme. It covers eligibility criteria, rules and benefits of this long-term residency scheme for investors and professionals seeking to settle in the Emirates.

items.title: H-1B visa fees could exceed $200,000 under reported Trump administration proposal
items.summary: A proposal under consideration by the Trump administration could raise H-1B visa fees to over two hundred thousand dollars. This potential increase would significantly impact Indian tech workers and their employers who sponsor these employment-based visas, though the change is not yet confirmed.

items.title: September 2026 Visa Bulletin warns some categories may run out before 30 September
items.summary: The US State Department has kept employment-based final action dates unchanged for September, but cautioned that EB-1 India, EB-2 and unreserved EB-5 could retrogress or become unavailable as annual limits are reached before the fiscal year closes. EB-2 remains unavailable for applicants born in India. Anyone whose date is current should be filing now rather than waiting.

items.title: New public charge standard from 18 September, immigrant visa interviews paused for officer training
items.summary: USCIS form changes tied to a new public charge standard take effect on 18 September 2026. Separately, the State Department is temporarily pausing immigrant visa interview appointments worldwide while consular officers are trained on the new screening guidance. Applicants with scheduled interviews should watch for rescheduling notices rather than assume their date holds.

items.title: Family-sponsored cut-off dates advance sharply, some by more than two years
items.summary: Several family-sponsored categories moved forward significantly in the September bulletin, with advances of over two years in some cases. The department has attributed the movement to reduced immigrant visa issuance for certain nationalities. Practitioners note that consular capacity in the final month may limit how many of those numbers actually get used.

items.title: Express Entry keeps favouring category-based draws in shortage occupations
items.summary: Canada's Express Entry system continues to run category-based selection rounds aimed at healthcare, science and technology, engineering and skilled trades, rather than relying only on general draws. With Indian applicant volumes high, CRS scores have stayed competitive — most candidates are responding by improving language scores and documenting work experience more carefully.

items.title: UK keeps tighter dependant rules for several student categories
items.summary: The UK continues to restrict dependant visas for certain categories of international students as part of a wider migration control effort. Indian numbers remain strong regardless — the sponsored study visa acceptance rate for Indian applicants has been reported around 97 per cent. Post-study employment increasingly depends on a genuine job offer at a competitive salary.
